images.title: Xbox Adaptive Controller, top and the back edge's jacks
images.author: unreal-ng
images.terms: vector drawing from measured dimensions; photos used as references only, nothing traced

references.what: top view (orthographic within 1 %: 2.22 : 1 against the maker's 2.25 : 1): the slab, the two 100 mm pads, the D-pad, Xbox, View, Menu, the profile button and its lights, the labels along the top edge, the A / B marks; positions and sizes on a 5 mm grid and with blob fits
references.author: InclusiveGameLab
references.use: measured geometry only (positions on a grid); no pixels shipped
references.note: the lab's triangle sticker between the pads is left out

references.what: the back edge: 19 jacks of 3.5 mm with their grooves and labels, the connect button, USB-C, the 5 V DC barrel
references.author: InclusiveGameLab
references.note: drawn in the order of the top's labels (the edge seen through the device); spacing measured on the top's labels, the jacks' height on the edge estimated

references.what: the USB-A ports on the two short sides (a joystick there drives the left / right stick): drawn as slots at the ends of the strip, their place along the side estimated
references.source: https://learn.adafruit.com/diy-adaptive-game-controllers/adaptive-joysticks (the two USB ports for joysticks that stand in for the thumbsticks)
references.note: an estimate: one port at each end
